decisions.correction: Keep this composition: Nagoji in the rust-red turban, cream tunic and broad red sash, centred behind the king's red-cushioned seat in torch and lamp light, with Dhanaji (white pagdi, short black beard, indigo quilted tunic) on his right and two off-white-turbaned riders on each side, plus the plain unlettered red banner and the open night pavilion. decisions.correction: Keep the high view looking down from the ridge, the copper sunset, the Maravar riders splashing knee-deep through the shallows and the Dutch ships offshore exactly as composed, but replace the carts. decisions.correction: Make this a true reverse angle. Show no lit lanterns anywhere, so the glints read clearly as glass. Keep the ship's dark hull, painted gunport strake, rigging and plain red-white-blue ensign (no monogram or lettering) as drawn, with the ship lying at anchor or barely moving, and keep a band of open sky in the upper left clear for two balloons.

Because NAGOJI has a line here, readers will take him for Nagoji, which breaks the clean-shaven chin and the commander sheet (no turban, no tunic or sash). The hall behind is a seated crowd rather than the emptying hall of 20.1. Ramayyan is on screen-left, which reverses the left/right staging of 20.1 and 20.5 (Nagoji left, Ramayyan right).
decisions.correction: Show ONLY Ramayyan in this frame, matching his sheet: thin, sharp features, receding curly hair, plain white cloth. Frame him as a medium close shot, seated cross-legged on the woven mat on the RIGHT half of the frame, head bowed, eyes on the bound palm-leaf bundle in his left hand, stylus in his right, not looking up. Use the same dusk hall as 20.1: dark wooden pillars, tiled roof, lit brass oil lamps, one side open to a purple-and-orange dusk sea with palms. Do NOT draw any second person seated beside or near him. That means no bearded man, no bare-chested man, no topknot, no rudraksha beads and no red-bordered cloth on a companion. Nagoji is off-panel to the LEFT. At most the edge of a cream sleeve and a plain red sash may cut in at the left frame edge, with no face, head or beard visible. The hall behind is nearly empty: at most two or three small chiefs in white mundu, backs turned, walking out toward the open side, never a seated crowd. Keep the upper left and upper centre (plain wall or dusk sky) clear and low-detail for two balloons. No text, letters or pseudo-text anywhere.

decisions.issues: Ramayyan matches his sheet and shows the dry, thin smile; his hands, stylus and leaves are sound, and there is no text. The large plain wall at right is ideal for both balloons. Minor: about eight people still sit in the background by the sea-side railing, so the hall is fuller than the empty hall of 20.1, though it still reads as lingering at dusk. A woman with jasmine in a maroon sari is among them; the hall's earlier crowds have similar women, so she does not read as Revathi. The soft, headless foreground shoulder at left (white garment with a red band edged in orange) reads acceptably as the listening Nagoji, though his sash is normally plain red.

Tight shot of Ramayyan's weathered hand closing over a few peppercorns on the woven mat, as scripted. The hand anatomy is sound, and the reaching forearm is long but plausible under foreshortening. There is no text, and the setting matches the same dusk hall. Minor: a brass bowl of peppercorns has been added in the foreground, and the leaf bundle in his other hand is drawn as thin strips. The empty mat at lower right and the dusk sky at upper right can take the single off-panel line. Ramayyan's head is out of frame at top left.

All hard checks pass. Nagoji's stud is a tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging, and he has a thick moustache with no beard; his fist rests at the chin. He is barefoot, with sleeves down and the commander sheet. Ramayyan matches his sheet and holds a single leaf whose edges are dark with handling, as scripted. There is no text and the lamplit hall matches 20.1. Minor: Nagoji's talwar is not visible, and a small red cloth corner shows by Ramayyan's far knee. There is room for four balloons in the upper wall and roof band: the plain wall above and left of Nagoji's turban and between the centre pillars, plus the roof and sky at upper right above Ramayyan.

Passes the hard checks: commander sheet, boots, sleeves down, no brand showing, talwar at the hip, thick moustache, shaven chin with only faint shading, four clusters of light with no masts, no text, and sound hands. Minor points: the ear ornament is a small gold ball sitting low on the lobe with a tiny cap. It touches the lobe and does not dangle, so it reads as a stud at print size. The background watchman is not clearly older. His dark vest and hand torch do not match the watchman in 21.4. Open sky at top right takes both captions.

Acceptable. The Goa ghost has the vaulted stone wall, the brazier and the table with iron tools. There are no ropes, no noose and no figures. Ear studs are flush on the lobe. Sleeves are down. Minor points: five clusters of ship lights here against four in 21.1, 21.3, 21.4 and 21.5. He gazes up and to the right, away from the lights, so the lights are not really in his eyes. This close-up shows light stubble on the chin and jaw; it is not a beard, but it goes past the bible's clean-shaven ideal. Open night sky at top left takes both captions.

FAIL on the brand: the arm planted on the rock is his RIGHT arm. That hand is palm down, thumb on the viewer's right, and is the near arm on the screen-left side of his body. Its sleeve is rolled up, and the scar mark is on the back (outer) side of the right forearm. The bible requires the edge of the brand on the INNER LEFT forearm only, with the right sleeve down. FAIL on framing: the script asks for a close insert of the palm pressed on rock with ridged nails, but this is a full-figure seated shot with a small hand. The nails also look smooth, not ridged. Everything else is fine: tiny flush ear stud, clean chin, boots and night setting.
decisions.correction: Frame this as a tight insert, not a full figure. The camera is low and close at his LEFT side, slightly in front. His LEFT hand and forearm fill most of the panel. The left hand is planted flat on the rough, lichen-flecked bluff rock just behind and beside his left hip, fingers spread and pointing backward, away from the camera, as if he leans back a little. The palm is pressed hard into the stone. The knuckles and the uneven, ridged fingernails are sharp in the foreground. Because the fingers point backward, the pale INNER (palm-side) surface of the left forearm faces the camera. The cream LEFT sleeve is eased back only a little past the wrist. A hand's width above the wrist, half hidden at the cuff's edge, just the edge of an old pale puckered patch of raised scar ridges shows. It has no letters, no numerals and no cross. Put no mark on the back of the hand, on the outer forearm or on the right arm. His right arm is not shown, or stays fully sleeved. At one edge show only a sliver of the cream trouser knee and the red sash. The light is cool night moonlight, with the four small clusters of ship lights soft and out of focus beyond the rock edge. Keep the upper third as dark open sky or shadowed rock for two speech balloons. No face is needed in this panel.

decisions.issues: Acceptable. Faint haze over the second of four clusters of lights. Nagoji's head is turned toward it with brows drawn and eyes narrowed. Boots, sleeves down, no brand, clean chin with faint shading, no text. Minor points: the framing repeats the medium-wide of 21.1 rather than putting his head in the near foreground, and his nostrils are not clearly flared. The ear ornament is a gold ball with a tiny cap at the bottom of the lobe. It touches the lobe and does not dangle, but it is borderline against the flush-stud rule. The watchman's look (white turban, sleeveless cream tunic, fire bowl on a wall) differs from 21.1's watchman. Wide open sky at top centre and right takes all three captions.

FAIL on framing: the script asks for a far pull-back with a TINY figure on the bluff. Here Nagoji fills nearly half the panel height in the mid-ground, a scale close to 21.1 and 21.4, so the closing image loses its sense of a small man against the coast. Everything else is fine: four clusters of light with no masts, the long coastline, boots, sleeves down, shaven chin and a small ear ornament. The coast is also dotted with several village lamps, though the script calls for a long dark coast.
decisions.correction: Pull the camera much further back and higher, as an extreme wide shot. Nagoji must be a tiny figure, no taller than about one eighth of the panel height. He is a small seated silhouette with a speck of rust-red turban and cream clothes, knees drawn up, at the very edge of the bluff in the left third of the frame. Keep the long dark coastline curving away into the far distance, with no village lamps or only one faint one. Keep the black sea filling most of the width, the moon and its glitter on the water, the night sky with thin cloud, and exactly four small clusters of ship lights on the sea with no masts or hulls visible. Leave a clear band of open sky across the top for one caption. No watchman, no other figures, no text.
